rules.title: Accordion — paired `<button aria-expanded>` + `aria-controls`
Alert — `role="alert"` for time-sensitive, transient announcements
Alertdialog — `role="alertdialog"` requires name + describedby + focus trap
Combobox — input + popup with full ARIA pattern
Dialog (Modal) — focus trap + initial focus + Esc + return focus
Disclosure — `<button aria-expanded>` toggling a region
Listbox — `role="listbox"` + `role="option"` + `aria-selected`
Menu / Menubar — `role="menu"` + `role="menuitem"` + roving-tabindex
Menu Button — `<button aria-haspopup aria-expanded aria-controls>`
Radio Group — `<fieldset><legend>` or `role="radiogroup"` with name
Slider — `role="slider"` + `aria-valuemin/max/now` + `aria-valuetext` where needed
Switch — `role="switch"` + `aria-checked`
Tabs — `role="tablist"` + `role="tab"` + `role="tabpanel"` + roving tabindex
Toolbar — `role="toolbar"` + arrow-key + roving tabindex
Tooltip — `role="tooltip"` + `aria-describedby` + hover + focus + Esc
Tree View — `role="tree"` + `role="treeitem"` + `aria-expanded` / `aria-level`

Do not put `aria-hidden="true"` on focusable elements or their ancestors

Dates use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with explicit locale (never hardcoded `MM/DD/YYYY` or `DD/MM/YYYY`)
Numbers use `Intl.NumberFormat` with explicit locale (never hardcoded `1,000.00` or `1.000,00`)
Currency uses `Intl.NumberFormat({style: "currency"})` with explicit currency code (never hardcoded `$` prefix or assumed-USD display)
Relative time uses `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (never hardcoded "3 hours ago" / "in 2 days" English phrasing)
Joining lists of items uses `Intl.ListFormat` (never hardcoded `", "` + English `"and"` / `"or"`)
Language / region / script / currency display-names use `Intl.DisplayNames` (never hardcoded English "German" / "France" / "Latin")
Text segmentation (grapheme/word/sentence) uses `Intl.Segmenter` (never `String.prototype.split(" ")` or per-character iteration)
Locale tag handling uses `Intl.Locale` for canonical BCP 47 manipulation (never substring-based parsing)
Date storage + transport in UTC; display in user's IANA timezone (never `new Date()` arithmetic in local TZ)
Locale detection prefers explicit user preference; falls through to `Accept-Language` server-side / `navigator.languages` client-side (never trust `navigator.language` alone)
`<html dir="rtl">` is set when the active locale is RTL (auto-mirror entry-point)
Use CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, etc.) instead of physical properties
Inline bidi isolation for opposite-direction embedded text — use `<bdi>` or `dir="auto"` (never naïve concatenation)
Directional icons mirror under RTL; non-directional icons do NOT mirror
Use HTML bidi markup (`<bdi>` / `dir`) — never bare Unicode bidi control characters (U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069)
Form-control alignment respects `dir` attribute — native controls auto-handle; custom controls need explicit logical alignment
Dir-attribute propagation crosses SPAs / iframes / shadow-DOM boundaries on locale change
Prefer HTML `dir` attribute over CSS `direction` property for typical RTL toggling
RTL-aware animations + transforms — slide-in originates from logical-inline-start (`translateX` mirrors under RTL)
Mixed-direction layouts — global nav LTR + RTL content (or vice versa) via per-region `dir` attribute + bidi isolation
All user-facing strings must use a translation function (no hardcoded language)
Pluralization must use CLDR-aware library (NOT `if count === 1` or `count !== 1`)
Runtime `<html lang>` value matches the active user-language locale (composes with A11Y-001)
Gender / grammatical agreement uses ICU `select` (not English-only conditionals)
Never concatenate translated fragments — use a single message with placeholders
Locale fallback chain follows CLDR parent-locale inheritance — never English-as-default for non-English locales

Missing-translation handling must signal the defect — never silently render empty / fallback-to-English-only
Message keys use stable namespaced identifiers — never embed presentation data or feature-prefix branding
